result.summary: Locks the blocks directory inside BlockManager using an RAII lock member rather than relying solely on bitcoind's init. This prevents external or kernel consumers from opening and overwriting an active node's block files.
result.problem: Only bitcoind's init took a lock on the blocks directory, leaving libbitcoinkernel and standalone kernel binaries without directory locks. A kernel binary run against a running node's blocks directory with a separate or in-memory datadir would silently open blk00000.dat in "rb+" mode and overwrite existing blocks from offset 0.
evidence: PR description: 'It starts without error, but with an empty block index BlockManager writes from offset 0 of the node's blk00000.dat, which FlatFileSeq::Open opens in place with "rb+". The node keeps running and serves the overwritten bytes as its own blocks.'
Review discussion in merged #31674 noted that 'the kernel does not currently do any dir locking, but it should', suggesting the lock be taken in BlockManager.
result.scope_notes: Moves blocksdir directory lock ownership into BlockManager's lifecycle and adds a test in feature_filelock.py using bitcoin-chainstate.
result.card: Moves the blocks directory lock into BlockManager so that all kernel consumers acquire it automatically. Previously, only bitcoind's init locked the blocks directory, allowing kernel tools pointing at a running node's blocksdir to overwrite blk00000.dat in place and corrupt block storage. Following up on merged PR 31674, this PR prevents concurrent processes from corrupting block data.

risk.why: A bug in directory locking or lifetime management could cause bitcoind or kernel consumers to fail startup or fail to release locks on restart or reindex.
